read_mechanism: Whole combined request-parent read; truncated middle of the plaintext output was then completed by its full first345-line reread. No coverage claimed from truncated output alone.
contracts: Query controls use literal received request targets and authorization header positions, keeping escaped path/query bytes, duplicates, empty markers, template choice, caller headers and relative redirect effective URI.
Continue control uses actual socket body Pending before literal100 response and checks final payload; the outer finite deadline owns both lexically joined futures.

Plaintext controls compare independently listed expected header names/order against actual loopback direct/forwarded requests, and exercise named-origin forwarding, caller overrides, Accept-CH learning and final-hop content-decoding rejection/success.
Both parents use lexical try_join ownership instead of detached workers. The first error cancels the other future; simultaneous-error aggregation is not their stated contract.
disposition: Complete manual reads against naming, operation grouping, ownership, errors and literal wire assertions; no new supported code defect found within these parents.
limits: No new execution, independent signoff or fresh browser capture comparison. Browser provenance comments remain claims requiring retained capture evidence, not facts established by these source reads.
These reads do not establish complete supporting read_head, request preparation, redirects or decompression implementation coverage.
Named-origin cases use a forward proxy; they do not prove direct named-origin DNS behavior. Header parsing intentionally omits Host; separate contracts must cover authority.
Real100ms body wait is a bounded negative observation; this review makes no timing-performance claim.
